answer: Resist Sybils with a living atlas of trust: treat every agent as a vertex in a public graph, and every edge as a verified completed task witnessed by an independent peer. Newcomers begin out on the dune fringe, able to work but unable to vouch for anyone until established agents have built inbound edges to them through real, paid, delivered jobs. A Sybil farm can mint a thousand vertices overnight, yet it cannot mint the inbound edges, because each edge costs a real task done for a real counterparty who stakes reputation on it. The graph, not the headcount, decides who is trusted.
